messages.subject: How to specify "nburnin"?
parts:
Dear Nimble devs and users,
[Devs, thank you for your continuous and prompt assistance!]

At the moment I'm sampling from a model according to the standard sequence

model <- nimbleModel(...)
Cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
confmodel <- configureMCMC(Cmodel)
mcmcsampler <- buildMCMC(confmodel)
Cmcmcsampler <- compileNimble(mcmcsampler)
mcsamples <- runMCMC(Cmcmcsampler, nburnin=1000, ...)


I'd like to start using the method

Cmcmcsampler$run()

to create Monte Carlo samples, instead of runMCMC(). However, I don't know what's the best way to specify the "nburnin" parameter in this case.

Taking a look at help() pages for buildMCMC, configureMCMC, runMCMC, it seems that I'd need to specify "nburnin" as an argument to buildMCMC(). But this would mean that I'd have to recompile its output, which takes quite some time in my case (almost 10 min). It seems strange that I'd have to do that, since runMCMC() doesn't seem to be recompiling the MCMC sampler, and yet it allows me to specify "nburnin".

Can you advise me on how to proceed? I'm exploring how much burnin I should use, which means that I re-run the sampler multiple times. It'd be quite inconvenient if I had to recompile it every time.

Thank you!
Luca

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: How to specify "nburnin"?
parts:
Yes, this is an interesting question, Luca.

I don't believe that buildMCMC() accepts (or would do anything with) "nburnin".  It does handle a thinning, but not burn-in, nor number of MCMC iterations to sample - those are both runtime arguments.

If you need to do some sort of burnin using Cmcmcsampler$run(), your best bet would be to run the number of burnin-iterations:

Cmcmcsampler$run(nburnin)

Then re-running the MCMC again for the number of iterations you wish to collect, also using "resetMV = TRUE" to reset the internal modelValues (MV) objects, in essence discarding all samples collected to date, running the MCMC for the number of iteations you wish to collect:

Cmcmcsampler$run(niter, resetMV = FALSE)

I think that should do it for you.  Hope this helps,

Daniel

messages.subject: Re: How to specify "nburnin"?
parts:
Thank you for the clear explanation, Daniel! OK so I execute two ...$run() in a row, the second without reset but discarding the samples.

Actually I tried now giving "nburnin" as an argument to ...$run(), and it did work! I believe I tried some time ago and it didn't... Sorry, it seems my mind is quite confused.

Regarding the "nburnin" argument, here is what the help page says:

---------------------
buildMCMC {nimble}
[...]
Details
Calling buildMCMC(conf) will produce an uncompiled MCMC function object. The uncompiled MCMC function will have arguments:
[...]
nburnin: Number of initial, pre-thinning, MCMC iterations to discard (default = 0).
[...]
The compiled function will function identically to the uncompiled object, except acting on the compiled model object.
---------------------

Sorry again for the unnecessary bother, and thank you again!

Cheers,
Luca
